**8B.4 Research Note**

**Positive / partial evidence**
- **Title:** Sheikh Hasina sworn in as PM for 5th term, forms 37-member cabinet  
  **Publisher:** BSS  
  **Date:** January 11, 2024  
  **URL:** https://b.bssnews.net/news-flash/167551  
  **Claim:** The cabinet included two technocrats, Yeafesh Osman and Samanta Lal Sen. That is limited but real evidence that Hasina did not rely entirely on party operatives and did place some capable specialists inside the executive.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** PM assigns charges to her 7 advisers  
  **Publisher:** The Daily Star  
  **Date:** January 21, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/pm-assigns-charges-her-7-advisors-3524926  
  **Claim:** The advisory circle included economists, academics, and a former principal secretary. That is stronger evidence of appointing people with administrative and technical competence, even though trusted insiders were also present.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Title:** Govt adopts plan to turn public welfare services into smart services in two years  
  **Publisher:** UNB  
  **Date:** June 4, 2024  
  **URL:** https://unb.com.bd/category/Bangladesh/govt-adopts-plan-to-turn-public-welfare-services-into-smart-services-in-two-years/136812  
  **Claim:** The government brought 52 ministries and divisions into a Smart Bangladesh implementation platform. That suggests Hasina was at least empowering a broad administrative network to execute a defined program.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Title:** Bangladesh receives $900 million World Bank financing to increase economic and urban resilience  
  **Publisher:** World Bank  
  **Date:** June 21, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/21/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-increase-economic-and-urban-resilience-for-sustainable-growth  
  **Claim:** The package included fiscal and financial-sector reforms, stronger banking oversight, procurement reform, and resilience spending. This is evidence that some competent administrators were being used to execute reform-linked policy.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** IMF Executive Board concludes the second review under Bangladesh’s ECF/EFF/RSF  
  **Publisher:** IMF  
  **Date:** June 24, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/24/pr24234-bangladesh-imf-exec-board-concludes-2nd-review-ecf-eff-rsf  
  **Claim:** The IMF said program performance was broadly on track and cited exchange-rate realignment, a crawling peg, tighter monetary policy, and tax/subsidy reforms. This is the best evidence that Hasina’s government could empower competent economic managers to carry out hard stabilization measures.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Title:** Advancing healthcare excellence: WHO’s role in developing the first national medical education strategy in Bangladesh  
  **Publisher:** WHO Bangladesh  
  **Date:** March 4, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh  
  **Claim:** The health ministry, with WHO support, used workforce studies and a technical working group to build a medical-education strategy. That is concrete evidence of empowering capable bureaucrats and expert processes in at least one sector.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Title:** 2nd JEE Bangladesh  
  **Publisher:** WHO  
  **Date:** July 11, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.who.int/southeastasia/news/detail/11-07-2024-2nd-jee-bn  
  **Claim:** Bangladesh completed a peer-reviewed Joint External Evaluation that identified strengths, gaps, and priority actions. This shows a functioning technical review mechanism and some willingness to empower expert correction inside the state.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority news on e-GP mandatory  
  **Publisher:** BPPA  
  **Date:** March 6, 2024  
  **URL:** https://bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1483.html  
  **Claim:** BPPA said the government was making e-GP mandatory and moving procurement onto a digital platform. That implies Hasina was empowering a rules-based administrative apparatus rather than leaving procurement entirely to informal loyalists.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh and partners support Rohingya and host communities  
  **Publisher:** World Bank  
  **Date:** May 28, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co  
  **Claim:** The project funded health, nutrition, education, shelters, livelihoods, and GBV prevention for Rohingya and host communities. This is positive but narrower evidence that capable delivery teams were being used to execute humanitarian policy.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.2

**Negative evidence**
- **Title:** New Cabinet Formation: Loyalists, fresh faces likely to get priority  
  **Publisher:** The Daily Star  
  **Date:** January 9, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/new-cabinet-formation-loyalists-fresh-faces-likely-get-priority-3515421  
  **Claim:** Contemporaneous reporting said the new cabinet would likely prioritize party loyalists and that technocrats would be rare. This points against a merit-first selection pattern and toward patronage as the default.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh PM Hasina secures fourth straight term in vote boycotted by main opposition  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint  
  **Date:** January 8, 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-pm-sheikh-hasina-secures-fourth-straight-term-in-vote-boycotted-by-main-opposition/1914659/  
  **Claim:** Reuters reported the BNP boycotted the vote after Hasina refused to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election. That is evidence she did not empower neutral professionals or institutions where they threatened regime control.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Title:** Bangladesh turnout low in election set to keep PM Hasina in power  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / Investing.com  
  **Date:** January 7, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-turnout-low-in-election-set-to-keep-pm-hasina-in-power-3268699  
  **Claim:** Reuters described the election as one designed to keep Hasina in power rather than a genuinely competitive contest. That suggests the ruler’s staffing and mobilization choices were subordinated to regime preservation.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Title:** Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / Investing.com  
  **Date:** July 22, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153  
  **Claim:** Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence. That is consistent with empowering coercive loyalists for crisis control rather than competent, independent executors.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh army refused to suppress protest, sealing Hasina’s fate  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / VOA  
  **Date:** August 7, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.voanews.com/a/exclusive-bangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasina-s-fate/7733166.html  
  **Claim:** Reuters reported the army would not fire on civilians to enforce Hasina’s curfew. This is strong counterevidence that she could not fully command coercive officials to execute her preferred response.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh’s internet shutdown isolates citizens, disrupts business  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / Investing.com  
  **Date:** July 26, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladeshs-internet-shutdown-isolates-citizens-disrupts-business-3539448  
  **Claim:** Reuters described a countrywide internet blackout used during the unrest, including a pattern of prior use around elections. That indicates operational capability, but toward suppression and survival rather than empowerment of capable public servants.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh blocks roads and internet, deploys army to curb protests  
  **Publisher:** Reuters  
  **Date:** July 20, 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/  
  **Claim:** Reuters described soldiers, roadblocks, and communications shutdowns during the crackdown. This shows the state could mobilize force, but the actors empowered were coercive administrators rather than program-capable reformers.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Al govt created lawless economy; crony capitalism captured public organizations  
  **Publisher:** The Daily Star  
  **Date:** October 31, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/al-govt-created-lawless-economy-3741796  
  **Claim:** A white-paper lead said authoritarian practices produced crony capitalism and a nexus of politicians, bureaucrats, and business interests that captured public organizations. That is strong evidence against empowering capable professionals over loyalists and patrons.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh PM Hasina reappoints son Sajeeb Wazed as honorary ICT adviser  
  **Publisher:** BSS  
  **Date:** January 21, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.bssnews.net/news-flash/169281  
  **Claim:** Hasina reappointed her son as honorary ICT adviser. Family-linked staffing is direct counterevidence to a clean meritocratic selection pattern.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.4, 8B.2

**Bottom line**
- **Best positive case:** Hasina did empower some capable people, especially in economic management, procurement reform, health planning, nuclear safety, and a few cabinet/advisory posts.
- **Best negative case:** The overall pattern still leaned toward loyalists, family-linked appointments, and coercive operators, with capable professionals used selectively and often inside tightly controlled or externally supervised channels.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a strong 2024 source showing systematic merit-based empowerment across the full cabinet, the security services, or the broader civil service. The clearest positive evidence is sectoral and partial; the clearest negative evidence is the persistent use of loyalists, family-linked appointments, and coercive control.
